title: Add deep-linked cost anchors and trace deblurring dashboard
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces deeplinkable cost anchors for per-token trace inspection and a Trace Deblurring dashboard that helps operators map aggregated token cost spikes back to specific spans, prompts, and token offsets. No API surface breaking changes. Migration: small backfill job to populate anchor IDs for last 7 days.
description: Motivation: long-tail cost and latency spikes are frequently buried in aggregated rollups. Engineers need a low-friction way to jump from a cost/latency spike in a per-route or per-tenant heatmap directly to the underlying trace segments and the token offsets that caused disproportionate cost. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: 1) a compact, stable 'cost anchor' added to invocation/span telemetry that lets dashboards generate deterministic deep links into traces and logs; 2) a Trace Deblurring dashboard that consumes anchors to visualize per-token contributions and to annotate the trace timeline with inferred token-boundaries and model-stage attributions. Summary of changes: - telemetry: add anchor_id (stable UUID) to invocation and span envelopes, plus token_offset metadata where available - tracing pipeline: new 'anchor indexer' that stores anchor->trace mapping and a tiny bloom filter for quick lookups - dashboard: new Trace Deblurring Grafana/Looker panel set and route-level anchor-sparkline widgets - API: small opt-in endpoint /v1/anchors/{anchor_id} that returns a compact trace pointer and canonical deep-link URL - sampling: sampled-span sampler exposes anchor_id so sampled traces link back to the index - migrations: backfill job to compute anchors for 7 days of recent telemetry (configurable) Checklist: [x] Telemetry schema + docs updated [x] Indexer service + tests [x] Dashboard panels and templating [x] API endpoint and integration tests [x] E2E storybook for deep link flows Implementation notes: anchors are generated at the invocation boundary by hashing (tenant_id, route, invocation_id, timestamp) and emitting a v4-stable hex string. For spans that can be token-attributed (streaming generation, chunked responses), we attach token_offset_start/token_offset_end to relevant spans. The anchor index stores: anchor_id -> trace_id, span_id, approximate token range, and a short flame-sparkline of per-token cost percentiles (compressed). The Trace Deblurring dashboard implements a hybrid query: rollups for the overview and the anchor index for drilldown; panels include a token contribution bar, trace timeline with token-boundary markers, and a compact callsite cost table. Rollout & safety: the feature is behind an observability feature flag (obs.deep_links) and the indexer runs at reduced retention by default. Backfill runs as a k8s job and is throttled. Privacy: anchor_id alone is opaque; we avoid including prompt text in the index. Related: ENG-4271 (observability spike RCA UX), OBS-92 (token-level attribution RFC).

review_comments: Jorge: Great direction. Two asks: add a note on retention costs for the indexer and make sure anchor generation is idempotent across retries.
